newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Roche names Humer chief operating officer. [CORRECTED 07:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Roche names Humer chief operating officer. [CORRECTED 07:50 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects headline and text from "names Humer to its executive committee").
Roche Holding AG said it had named Franz Humer chief operating officer as part of a reorganisation of its board and senior management.
Fritz Gerber remains chairman and chief executive.
"In addition to his post as head of the pharmaceuticals division, Franz B. Humer assumes additional responsibility for coordinating the operational areas," it said in a statement.
The heart of the executive committee now comprises Gerber, Henri Meier as chief financial officer, and Humer as chief operating officer.

Andres Leuenberger becomes full-time vice chairman of the board, but leaves the executive committee, where he had been Gerber's deputy. Rolf Haenggi was also appointed vice chairman of the board to succeed Lukas Hoffmann, who has retired.

Leuenberger, 58, is also president of the Swiss Federation of Trade and Industry. He will be responsible for "various functions in the Roche Group" and remains chairman of the Givaudan-Roure Group, Roche's fragrances and flavours division.
Roche said it was combining its pharmaceutical activities in Switzerland into a new "Pharma Schweiz" group headed by Markus Altwegg. Altwegg already sits on the executive committee.
The company did not say why Leuenberger was leaving the executive committee.

One official who asked not to be named said it would be highly speculative to view Humer as the heir apparent to Gerber, who at the age of 67 still keeps a firm grip on both the board and the executive committee.
"This shows very clearly that the president and chairman remains on top of both bodies," he said.
